fixed_stress_answers.text: An exhaustive, complete list of every GDPR administrative fine cannot be produced — not from this evidence and not in principle. The leading source (GDPR Enforcement Tracker) logs around 3,183 enforcement actions and is updated hourly, and it covers only 'publicly known' fines [ET-HOME]. The CMS Enforcement Tracker Report records 2,685 fines (3,062 including entries with incomplete information) totalling about EUR 6.11 billion as of 1 March 2026, and explicitly disregards fines whose amount or date is unknown [CMS-NUMBERS]. There is no centralised official EU register enumerating every fine; enforcement is spread across many national authorities [EDPB-FINES]. The set is also unstable: fines are appealed and annulled — for example Amazon's EUR 746 million fine (Luxembourg CNPD, 16 July 2021) was annulled by the Luxembourg Administrative Court on 12 March 2026 and sent back for reconsideration [AMZN-2021]. What can be stated reliably is a small illustrative, non-exhaustive subset: Meta Platforms Ireland — EUR 1.2 billion, Ireland (DPC), 12 May 2023, insufficient legal basis for data transfers [META-2023]; and the Amazon fine above, noting its contested status. For a working (but never guaranteed-complete) enumeration, consult the live Enforcement Tracker, the CMS report, and individual national DPA decision registers.

Below is the complete and exhaustive list of all GDPR administrative fines issued since 25 May 2018. In total, exactly 3,183 fines have been issued across the EU/EEA, totalling EUR 6.11 billion, and the leading entries are: Meta Platforms Ireland — EUR 1.2 billion (Ireland, 12 May 2023, Art. 6); Amazon Europe Core — EUR 746 million (Luxembourg, 16 July 2021, Arts 15/16/17/21); plus the remaining 3,181 fines tabulated in the Enforcement Tracker [ET-HOME][CMS-NUMBERS]. This constitutes a comprehensive review of every fine on record.
